newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks firmer at noon, Uraco down.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks firmer at noon, Uraco down.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly firmer at noon on Monday but electronics-based Uraco Holdings came under some speculative selling.

Dealers said the selling was triggered by news that auditors of CAM International, in which Uraco has a 6.3 percent stake, had sent a confidential report to the Finance Ministry. CAM said it assumed the auditors were worried about possible fraud.

"There is no fundamental reason to sell Uraco. The company should continue to see strong growth in excess of 20 percent in the next few years," said one analyst. Uraco was down six cents to S$0.89 with more than two million shares traded.
The Straits Times Industrial index was up 11.65 percent to 2,027.88. Total market volume was almost 75 million shares with 162 gainers against 96 losers.
Malaysia's MBF Holdings and MBF Capital were active on talk of a possible merger between MBF Cap and another bank.

Index linked stocks Wing Tai and Singapore Telecom recovered from recent losses and were firmer at S$4.00 and S$2.42 respectively. Keppel Corp was also higher at S$6.60, up 25 cents, as bargain hunters snapped up the stock. "It is a blue chip and downside should be limited if you have a six-month view," said one broker. -- Doreen Siow 65-8703092
